origin.note: tag v1.1.0; the vendored tree was subsequently rebased on upstream master at 65f234eb81 (2026-07-20), which lib/berry/src matches apart from the patches below (lib/berry/berry_conf.h)

patches.summary: berry_conf.h is the project's copy of upstream default/berry_conf.h with AWTRIX values
VM stack nil-fill, float constant tables outside ESP32 IRAM, idle-stack/trace release seam and newlib-nano printf handling, marked AWTRIX
AWTRIX Modbus module and registration from main 421eb23, with regenerated constant string tables for the script bindings
2026-09-26: bound integer-format length modifier insertion by the actual format buffer capacity and raise value_error before overflow (upstream issue berry-lang/berry#544).

2026-09-28: NUL-terminate leading-dot real literals before conversion (backport of upstream 6e6e6213, berry-lang/berry#546), and keep the token name table in enum order so syntax errors name the right keyword (still wrong upstream).

2026-10-03: backport of upstream 66d2d0f9 and 4bf803a5 (berry-lang/berry#549, #551) and of the register release from 997de1c7 (#553): a short-circuit result keeps its own register, so the call arguments after `a || b` are no longer shifted, an assignment to a nested index no longer releases a register that a local still holds, and `p := l[i]` as a call argument no longer shifts the arguments. From the rest of #553 only the refusal of a `:=` that would create a local over a pending temporary is taken; upstream refuses every variable created by `:=`.
compile i_savecode only with BE_USE_BYTECODE_SAVER, whose functions it calls, marked AWTRIX

2026-10-03: backport of upstream 6e6e6213 (berry-lang/berry#546) and 2c0b935c: parser depth limit (BE_MAX_PARSER_DEPTH in berry_conf.h), out-of-range jumps refused, string escapes bounded, string size capped, bytes() offsets checked without integer overflow and setbytes() clamped to the source, bytecode loader and debug.caller() hardened.

patches.summary: 2026-09-15 hardening: bounded line and header growth for requests, responses and trailers; chunked terminator required; malformed request headers close the socket
2026-09-25: a request with neither Content-Length nor chunked encoding has no body (RFC 9112 section 6.3) instead of being read until the peer closes

2026-09-26: preserve literal header values (CVE-2026-45372), consume bounded trailers separately from initial headers (CVE-2025-53628), backport iterative Content-Disposition/filename* parsing (CVE-2026-29076), reject signed chunk sizes (GHSA-h6wq-j5mv-f3q8), and omit exception detail headers (CVE-2026-28434). Based on upstream advisories and the v0.37.0 multipart parser.

2026-10-04: the client accepts response status and header lines that end in a bare LF (streamABC/regiocast and other radio servers) and Shoutcast's ICY 200 OK as HTTP/1.0; request and trailer parsing are unchanged
